## Final result

### Median family net wealth by cohort × year (complete-case, nominal USD)
| Cohort | 1985 | 1990 | 1996 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **White (NON-BLACK NON-HISPANIC proxy)** | $3,500 (n=5,774) | $12,972 (n=5,336) | $42,600 (n=3,557) |
| **Black** | $1,600 (n=1,699) | $4,800 (n=1,528) | $9,800 (n=1,368) |
| **Hispanic** | $500 (n=2,631) | $1,600 (n=2,431) | $2,562 (n=2,114) |

### White vs Black / White vs Hispanic — ratios and absolute differences (nominal)
| Year | W/B ratio | W/H ratio | W−B abs diff | W−H abs diff |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1985 | 2.19× | 7.00× | $1,900 | $3,000 |
| 1990 | 2.70× | 8.11× | $8,172 | $11,372 |
| 1996 | 4.35× | 16.62× | $32,800 | $40,038 |

Bootstrap 95% CIs (B=2000, complete-case) confirm non-overlap and widening: W/B ratio 1985: 1.84–2.47 → 1996: 3.73–5.29; W/H ratio 1985: 5.83–8.75 → 1996: 13.77–21.30; absolute differentials also strictly increase and never include zero.

### Trend across 1985 → 1990 → 1996
Both relative and absolute gaps **widened monotonically**: the W/B median ratio rose from 2.19× to 4.35× (~2.0× larger), the W/H ratio from 7.00× to 16.62× (~2.4× larger), while absolute gaps grew ~17× (Black) and ~13× (Hispanic) in nominal dollars. Even in real 1996 dollars (CPI-U), ratios are identical (scale-free) and absolute gaps grow from $2,771 / $4,375 (1985) to $32,800 / $40,038 (1996).

### Sensitivity — direction consistent with main result
- **Balanced panel** (n=5,739 with wealth in all three waves): W/B ratio 2.38 → 3.60 → 4.69 and W/H ratio 12.67 → 12.29 → 17.75. Direction (white > Black, white > Hispanic; overall widening 1985→1996) agrees with the main result. One small nuance: the balanced-panel W/H ratio is essentially flat (with a negligible dip) from 1985 to 1990 before rising sharply by 1996 — this does not change the headline conclusion.
- **Real-dollar** sensitivity: same conclusion.

### Missingness / attrition direction
Wealth missingness rose over time and is differential: NBNH 23%→29%→53%, Black 15%→24%→32%, Hispanic 17%→23%→33% (1985→1990→1996). If attrition is wealth-correlated (e.g., lower-wealth respondents more likely to be missing), magnitudes could be somewhat affected, but the direction of the disparity and of its widening is consistent across complete-case and balanced-panel analyses, so the qualitative conclusion is robust to this limitation.

### Final natural-language hypothesis
> In the NLSY79 data, treating the NON-BLACK NON-HISPANIC cohort as the proxy for "white" (the only racial/ethnic mapping the dataset supports), the median family net wealth of white individuals was substantially higher than that of both Black and Hispanic individuals in every observed wealth wave from 1985 onwards, and the gap widened over time. In nominal dollars the white median was about 2.2× the Black median in 1985 ($3,500 vs $1,600) and about 4.4× by 1996 ($42,600 vs $9,800), and about 7× the Hispanic median in 1985 ($3,500 vs $500) rising to about 16.6× by 1996 ($42,600 vs $2,562). The absolute white–Black median gap grew from roughly $1,900 to $32,800 and the white–Hispanic gap from roughly $3,000 to $40,038 (all nominal). These results are robust to a balanced-panel restriction and to inflation adjustment. Caveat: wealth non-response rose over time, reaching 53% missing for the Non-Black Non-Hispanic cohort by 1996 (vs ~32% Black, ~33% Hispanic); if attrition is wealth-related the magnitudes could differ somewhat, but the direction — white median net wealth above both Black and Hispanic medians in every year from 1985 onwards, with a widening gap — holds in both the main and sensitivity analyses.

payload.workflow: 1) Load nls_raw.csv (12,686 respondents). 2) Map cohort 3 -> White proxy (NON-BLACK NON-HISPANIC), cohort 1 -> Black, cohort 2 -> Hispanic. 3) Compute complete-case median Family net wealth per cohort per wave (1985/1990/1996). 4) Compute W/B and W/H median ratios and absolute differentials per wave; assess trend. 5) Sensitivities: balanced panel (all three waves present) and real 1996 USD via CPI-U. 6) Bootstrap 95% CIs (B=2000) on ratios/differentials. 7) Report differential missingness. All in analysis_wealth_disparity.py; output in analysis_output.txt.
